chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The beginning of the Aqeeq is Bareed al-Ba'as, and it is six miles from the Maslakh on the side facing Iraq, and between it and Ghamra are twenty-four miles, which is two Bareyds.
One of our companions said, 'When you exit from the Maslakh, enter into Ihram at the first Bareed that faces you.'

key_terms.أَحْرِمْ: Ahrim: Enter into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah).
key_terms.الْعَقِيق: Aqeeq: A specific station/place near Mecca used as a boundary for Ihram.
key_terms.الْمَسْلَخ: Al-Maslakh: A place or station from which one departs to enter the Ihram state.
key_terms.بَرِيدُ الْبَعْث: Bareed al-Ba'as: A specific distance marker or station, identified here as the beginning of the Aqeeq.
key_terms.غَمْرَة: Ghamra: Another station or location mentioned in relation to the distances of the Ihram boundary.

ai.seo_question: Where exactly should a pilgrim enter Ihram when traveling from Mecca to Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the Aqeeq as the designated Miqat for pilgrims from Iraq, situated six miles from the Maslakh, reflecting the early Shia scholarly emphasis on precise geographical markers for ritual purity. The mention of 'some of our companions' indicates a transmission of practical juristic application, ensuring pilgrims assume Ihram at the correct juncture to fulfill the Sunnah of the Prophet. This specific location underscores the importance of spatial sanctity in Hajj rituals within Shia fiqh.
